title: Rex Fleet Academy — Curriculum and Source-Text Adaptation Doctrine
corePromise: Rex Fleet Academy is about the transfer of consequential knowledge. The reader should watch an expert help serious trainees make a difficult fact about their universe visible, testable, debatable, and usable.

issueCountPolicy.rule: Academy courses are one-offs or very short limited series. Default to 1 issue; allow 2 or 3 only when the source material and dramatic form genuinely require it. Do not plan Academy courses as 6-, 8-, 10-, or open-ended issue seasons.
issueCountPolicy.existingPlans: Legacy numbered lecture plans beyond Issue 1 are idea inventories, not promised issues. Recast them as candidate modules that may be combined, omitted, or selected for at most two follow-up issues.
issueCountPolicy.productionBoundary: Only registered, compiled issue/page payloads are production authority. A course is complete after Issue 1 unless a second or third issue earns its existence.

sourceTextMethod.purpose: Let the world's own technical, historical, political, and geographic documents speak across the comic while instructors and cadets demonstrate, question, contextualize, and apply them.

captionLane.initialTarget: Approximately 6–9 short source-text lines per page, normally separated into individual caption boxes or clearly separated caption units.
captionLane.rule: This is a starting pacing range, not a quota. Page design, sentence length, art, dialogue, and dramatic rhythm may require fewer or more.
captionLane.speakerEncoding: When source text is adapted into production pages, encode it through assembler-visible CAPTION dialogue units, preserving exact approved wording and order.
captionLane.separation: Document voice and classroom voice are distinct. A teacher must not merely paraphrase or reread the caption track.

classroomLane: Demonstrate the source claim with apparatus, simulation, experiment, archival reconstruction, map work, field exercise, role-play, testimony comparison, or practical problem.
Use teaching analogies when they genuinely clarify the idea, then return to the precise model and show where the analogy breaks.
Let cadets make predictions, operate equipment, challenge premises, misread evidence, revise models, and experience consequences.
Prefer the moment of recognition—the student seeing why the source text matters—over passive exposition.
adaptationRules: Do not silently rewrite a source quotation into cleaner modern prose and still present it as the original document.
Before using source text verbatim, identify its authority, edition/version, era, and whether later canon supersedes or qualifies it.
If the source is development material rather than locked canon, label the adaptation lane accordingly until reconciliation is complete.
Long source passages should be selected and paced for dramatic usefulness; the comic is not required to reproduce every source line.
Use ellipsis or excerpt boundaries transparently in development notes when material is omitted; do not fabricate connective sentences inside a quoted document.
Teachers may disagree with, contextualize, or correct a source document when current evidence warrants it.

scienceEngineering.promise: Make invented physics and engineering observable, measurable, and operational.
scienceEngineering.visualGrammar: Future-college science and engineering: apparatus first, active manipulation, measurement, failure, correction, and student recognition. Avoid professor-at-podium staging and decorative pseudo-science.

historyPoliticalScience.promise: Teach how institutions, doctrines, and political settlements emerged from contested history rather than presenting current ideology as inevitable.
historyPoliticalScience.visualGrammar: Seminar plus reconstruction. Let source voices run over dramatized historical evidence; distinguish document, testimony, reconstruction, and Academy inference.

worldsCultureAtlas.promise: Teach places as lived systems: geography, trade, infrastructure, culture, political memory, and ordinary routines—not faction stereotypes.
worldsCultureAtlas.visualGrammar: Field study, map room, traveler briefing, comparative urbanism, and lived-world observation. Students should encounter places and people, not merely label regions on a map.

scienceNarrationExperiment.candidateSource: Reciprocal Field Transit & Asymptotic Inversion technical material
scienceNarrationExperiment.status: requires canon reconciliation and page-pacing test before becoming production text
scienceNarrationExperiment.proposedUse: Select coherent passages from the technical paper as a sustained narrator/source-caption track while Academy teachers and cadets perform the corresponding demonstrations, analogies, simulator work, and first-hand transit experience.
scienceNarrationExperiment.pacingTest: Prototype several representative pages at approximately 6–9 short caption lines per page, each line/beat in its own box or intentionally grouped unit; evaluate art breathing room, dialogue competition, reader speed, and whether equations need dedicated space.

dramatizationCandidate.beat: A trainee experiences reciprocal-field transit for the first time and feels the counterintuitive transition as thrust demand falls while velocity rises.
dramatizationCandidate.sourceStatus: Recovered development beat; preserve the scene idea, but reconcile final trainee/instructor identities before production.
dramatizationCandidate.function: Convert the paper's equations and analogy into lived bodily experience, so the reader feels the physics before or while understanding it.

sourceCriticism.rule: Academy instruction teaches provenance as well as content. A document may be accurate, partial, propagandistic, obsolete, later reinterpreted, or factually wrong.
sourceCriticism.physicalLaw: Scientific truth is not culturally relative. Different schools and regions may hold different models or empirical practices, but observation and consequences constrain them.
sourceCriticism.history: Historical sources may conflict without the story pretending that all claims are equally supported. Preserve uncertainty where the record is genuinely unresolved.

canonReconciliation.principle: Do not use the Academy format to paper over contradictions. Reconcile source authority before presenting disputed material as settled instruction.
workingPriority: Released StarSplitterVisions canon within its scope
Current production-authoritative RexPrompt data within its scope
Recovered foundational documents and development material
Older superseded drafts and public-wiki variants
canonReconciliation.crossProjectRule: Shattering of the Corridors is a standalone direct dramatic series and retains authority over the events it depicts in its own era. It is not an Academy course. A separate future Academy history topic may study those events retrospectively, while present-day Rex Fleet retains authority over its own era. Academy adaptations must not silently transfer ownership or overwrite either.

coverDoctrine.rule: Academy covers sell an intellectually irresistible act of learning.
coverDoctrine.preferredImage: Instructor + active learner(s) + one compelling demonstration, reconstruction, document, map, experiment, or field problem. The viewer should wonder what the students are discovering.
avoid: infrastructure-only spectacle when the learning event can carry the idea

externalSeriesBoundary.shattering: Shattering of the Corridors is not part of Rex Fleet Academy. It follows its characters directly as events unfold in real time. A future Academy history topic about the Shattering may be developed separately, but is not currently created or registered.

lineArchitecture.model: Umbrella imprint of self-contained Academy courses, not one continuous Academy season.
lineArchitecture.entryPointRule: Every course Issue 1 must function as a valid entry point both to that subject and to the Rex Fleet Academy line. It may assume the shared world, but not prior Academy-course reading.
lineArchitecture.lengthRule: Default to one issue. Use two or three only when the subject genuinely needs additional dramatic or source-text room. Three issues is the expected upper bound for a single course.
lineArchitecture.castRule: Courses may and often should use different instructors, cadets, technicians, historians, pilots, or field specialists suited to the subject. No recurring Academy ensemble is required across the line.
lineArchitecture.packageRule: Each course remains its own RexPrompt series ID and data package. Do not combine course character shelves, issue payloads, settings, or production state into one giant Academy package.
lineArchitecture.imgRule: Each course should have its own IMG project / visual-reference namespace when it enters image production. Cross-course visual references are explicit parent/shared references, not shared uncontrolled project state.
lineArchitecture.branchRule: Use course-specific short-lived development branches when editing RexPrompt, then merge approved work to main. Do not use long-lived Git branches as competing canon; main remains the durable repository authority.
